title: Pacts likely real, but does the verse mean them?

phrase.meaning: their custom of the winter and summer journey

points.label: Real pacts behind it
points.text: Ibn Saʿd, Ibn Ḥabīb and others tell of **Hāshim and his brothers** winning safe-conduct from rulers and tribes. Kister reads īlāf as **profit-sharing deals**, a “Pax Meccana” that made the journeys secure.

points.label: Real, but not the verse
points.text: Crone: “there is **no reason to think** that this verse alludes to any such arrangement.” The story is “wrong as exegesis”, yet such agreements were “likely… a **genuine Arabian institution**”, and Quraysh may well have used them.

points.label: A rebuke, not a gift
points.text: Rubin reads īlāf as **preoccupation**: Quraysh are too taken up with trade, though God already feeds the sanctuary. The call to worship becomes **a call back to the House**.

bottom_text: No consensus. Kister and Crone both find such pacts plausible; still open is whether the surah’s īlāf names them, or later tradition read them into the word.
source_label: Crone, BSOAS 70 (2007) · Kister, JESHO 8 (1965) · Rubin, Arabica 31 (1984)
